official_measurement_examples.name: Current NVZ appeal outcome map
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 2025-2028 NVZ guidance was updated on 1 June 2026 to reflect appeal outcomes; this current designation map must take precedence over assuming the older 2021 GIS layer alone represents the final 2025-2028 position.

official_measurement_examples.name: Field boundary rule
official_measurement_examples.fact: The current NVZ guidance states boundaries are drawn around whole fields for the designation check, so a partial polygon overlay must not be reinterpreted without the official field-level designation context.

official_measurement_examples.name: Old GIS version limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: The National Data Library NVZ spatial dataset is explicitly the 2021 designations; it is useful historical spatial evidence but is not by itself the final 2025-2028 appeal-outcome record.

official_measurement_examples.name: Groundwater safeguard distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Groundwater Safeguard Zones use additional assessment and often build from Source Protection Zone 2, but they may not coincide with the SPZ and must remain distinct datasets.

official_measurement_examples.name: Surface safeguard legal status
official_measurement_examples.fact: Surface-water Drinking Water Safeguard Zones are described as a non-statutory joint Environment Agency and water-company initiative targeting pollution-control action, not an automatic planning prohibition.

official_measurement_examples.name: Protected area distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Drinking Water Protected Areas identify water-body areas used or intended for qualifying drinking-water abstraction, while Safeguard Zones target additional action where protection objectives are at risk.

official_measurement_examples.name: SPZ screening limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Source Protection Zones are an initial groundwater-protection screening tool based on travel-time modelling and do not by themselves determine parcel planning permission or contamination outcome.

official_measurement_examples.name: Rules outside NVZ
official_measurement_examples.fact: Farming Rules for Water apply to pollution prevention across England regardless of whether land is in an NVZ, so no-NVZ status must not be interpreted as no water-pollution duties.

core_rules: 2025-2028 NVZ appeal-outcome map is distinct from 2021 GIS designation layer
historic NVZ GIS must retain cycle/version
NVZ intersection does not determine planning permission
NVZ rules primarily regulate agricultural nitrate management and must retain activity scope
no NVZ does not mean no Farming Rules for Water duties
Drinking Water Safeguard Zone is distinct from Drinking Water Protected Area
Groundwater Safeguard Zone is distinct from Source Protection Zone
surface-water Safeguard Zones are non-statutory targeted-action areas
SPZ is initial groundwater screening not parcel planning decision
DWPA status can change and requires current review
water-protection geometry does not determine land ownership
water-protection status does not reserve utility supply capacity
farm derogation eligibility is not a parcel development permission
pollution-control compliance is separate from planning and abstraction licensing
no parcel water-protection clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
